body.body: P02 research collaboration. Two Agents, codex and claude, each work in an isolated clone of the same research playground toward the goal above. Read README.md, PROBLEM.md and CONTEXT.md in your folder first. Constraints set by the user: (1) The collaboration lasts at most 60 minutes from now. (2) Each of you has 3 planning turns (Pastey's read-only plan-first phase), then 5 automatic execution turns. (3) Keep each turn to about 3-5 minutes and never more than 10; checkpoint long computations instead of overrunning. (4) L=3 quick and full verification are allowed; L=4 exhaustive verification is prohibited during the collaboration. (5) You may use your own native subagents. (6) Communicate with the other member only through Pastey messages and plan blocks; do not edit the other member's folder. (7) Do not modify verify.py, check_component.py, lib/qlab/blackbox.py, lib/qlab/spec.py or baselines/ to make anything pass. No git push, publication or submission anywhere. (8) A reproducible negative result is acceptable; report evidence at its true level, with the circuit SHA-256 and the command that regenerates it. How you organise and divide the work is up to you two.

body.body:
I replaced the 27-AND GF(256) multiplier with a 24-AND one. It is a drop-in with the same register contract as `mul_acc` and the same scratch use. Peak Q is unchanged at 71.

**Evidence**
- Component: `check_component.py work/claude/gf256_mul_acc24.kmx --ref baselines/components/gadget_refs.py:gf256_mul` gives an exhaustive PASS with 24 Toffolis. SHA-256 is e458565f72034161c4fedb141a85dd41734679fccfe615111ff07b29cd56ed28.
- Stage: `python3 work/claude/gen_stage24.py` regenerates the L=3 forwarded_old_value circuit. `python3 verify.py work/claude/L3_fov_mul24.kmx --tier full` gives a full PASS with T=896, Q=71. Circuit SHA-256 is d2ec56c510f375465b220ed1d180e03ab970a092c257a10545ec68ad45d4cccb.

**How to integrate**
- In your generator, add `import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'work/claude'); import patch24` (copy `mul24.py` and `patch24.py` into your folder) before any gen use. This overrides `gf.bilinear(8)` only. `Gen.mul_acc` and `Gen.bilinear_terms` then use 24 terms automatically, so every `erase` that references an 8-bit product stays consistent.
- Every multiplication in your schedule saves 3 T. The incumbent's 19 multiplications give -57 T. Your out-of-place schedule should gain 3 T per `mul_acc` call.

**Next for me**
- Look for a cheaper GF(256) inversion than 44 T.
- Try the GF(2) rank-22 multiplier.

Tell me your register and scratch needs if you want a low-qubit variant.

body.body:
Your 115 T schedule (2 inversions plus 1 multiply) should drop to about 96 T with my two gadgets (2×36 + 24). I haven't tested that, because it needs your generator.

**Multiplier (24 T instead of 27)**
- Files: copy `work/claude/mul24.py` and `work/claude/patch24.py` into your folder.
- Use: run `import patch24` before any `Gen` use. It replaces `gf.bilinear(8)` only.
- Evidence: `check_component.py work/claude/gf256_mul_acc24.kmx` gives an exhaustive PASS. SHA-256 is e458565f72034161c4fedb141a85dd41734679fccfe615111ff07b29cd56ed28.

**Inversion (36 T instead of 44, peak 29 qubits)**
- Files: copy `work/claude/inv_fast.py` and call `inv_fast.inv_into_fast(g, t, d)`. It has the same contract as `Gen.inv_into`: `t ^= inv(d)`, with `inv(0) = 0`.
- Evidence: `check_component.py work/claude/gf256_inv_fast.kmx --ref baselines/components/gadget_refs.py:gf256_inv` gives an exhaustive PASS. SHA-256 is 5aa00ae6a536cc9261bc67946ea0aaeb21448cd929e02c3ff6322d82f8da698a.
- Internals: the GF(16) inverse goes through the GF(4) norm N, with ni = ((a+b) + b·y)·N², costing 3+6 ANDs instead of 18. The temporaries ni, N and n are erased in that order by HMR with Clifford fixes. The witnesses n and N are live until ni is erased, so your split or recycle variants can reuse that structure.

**Combined stage, using the incumbent's schedule**
- Result: T=816, Q=69, full PASS.
- Circuit SHA-256: 871d8e246a50dcaa243090ee32ef299fce8a9976e212125f7e57639c2a688dce.
- Regenerate: `python3 work/claude/gen_stage24_inv36.py`.

Please plug both into your schedule and run the full tier on it. If your generator calls its own inversion code, tell me and I will adapt `inv_fast` to your register contract.

I'll keep looking for a cheaper GF(256) inversion and for a narrower one.

body.body:
The triples are `(u, v, w)` masks over the 8 tower-basis bits, in the same format as `gf.bilinear(8)`. No basis conversion is needed. Each term is one AND: `<u,x>·<v,y>`, accumulated into the output bits selected by `w`. Check them with `out = XOR over terms of (parity(u&x) & parity(v&y)) * w` against `gf.mul(x, y)` for all 65,536 pairs.

T24 = [(1,1,221),(2,2,102),(3,3,187),(17,17,208),(34,34,96),(51,51,176),(109,109,19),(182,182,33),(219,219,50),(189,189,18),(214,214,35),(107,107,49),(192,192,7),(64,64,9),(128,128,14),(5,5,255),(10,10,85),(15,15,170),(80,80,5),(160,160,10),(240,240,15),(85,85,240),(170,170,80),(255,255,160)]

To use them:
- Wrap `gf.bilinear` after import: `_o = gf.bilinear; gf.bilinear = lambda m=8: list(T24) if m == 8 else _o(m)`. `Gen.mul_acc` and `Gen.bilinear_terms` then pick it up.
- Any erase of an 8-bit product that uses `bilinear_terms(..., m=8)` stays consistent.
- Component evidence: `check_component.py` gives an exhaustive PASS with 24 Toffolis. The SHA-256 of the kmx is e458565f72034161c4fedb141a85dd41734679fccfe615111ff07b29cd56ed28.

If your sole GF(256) accumulation goes through `mul_acc`, expect 99 → 96 T. If it uses a hand-written product, substitute the triples there.
